editorialMeter.label: Neutral editorial anchor · no justified directional preference
editorialMeter.method: VC-010 methodological reset from unsupported inherited 59 to neutral display 50, correcting old unsourced +9 without changing observed physics. This is not 50% chance and the -9 is not evidence for a single history. All VC-001–009 original history retained. Future directional movement requires an actual model-discriminating comparison for one-vs-many physically realized histories; claim-specific experiments must independently change the ledger even if this compass remains neutral.
editorialMeter.empiricalVerdict: Unresolved count of actually real histories. Benchmark Markovian CSL physical-collapse parameters have been experimentally constrained and some excluded; that is a concrete model-specific conclusion. Everett and Bohm quantum equilibrium still share ordinary tested Born statistics. Neutral 50 is an uncalibrated display anchor, never odds.

entries.title: Gravitational time dilation is experimentally established
entries.direction: Neutral
entries.strength: High for time dilation, none for timeline count
entries.question: Can gravity change the passage of time?
entries.finding: Precision atomic clocks confirm relativistic time dilation. This does not demonstrate backward travel or multiple histories.
entries.source: NIST · Putting Einstein to the Test
entries.locationType: Associated institution; not a claimed experiment coordinate
entries.notes: Do not conflate established time dilation with the ability to alter the past.

entries.title: Closed timelike curves arise in some relativistic solutions
entries.direction: Neutral
entries.strength: Conditional / not physically observed
entries.question: Can general relativity admit looping worldlines?
entries.finding: Certain mathematical spacetimes contain closed timelike curves, but physical realizability and formation remain open.
entries.source: Gödel (1949) rotating cosmological solution; Hawking (1992) contrast
entries.notes: Original Gödel paper §1 p.447 and §3 p.449 constructs closed timelike paths in a specified rotating spacetime. Hawking studies constraints on forming chronology horizons from specified initial conditions, not a contradiction. Mathematical existence is not a measured machine or multiple histories. Follow-up limited independent algebra reproduced Gödel's g_phi_phi=4a²sinh²r(sinh²r−1), timelike for r>asinh(1); still only a conditional exact metric.

entries.title: Chronology protection is an unproven possibility
entries.direction: Neutral
entries.strength: Conjecture
entries.question: Might nature prevent paradox-causing time loops?
entries.finding: Hawking argues that compactly generated Cauchy horizons from bounded local interventions encounter classical energy-condition and quantum backreaction obstacles. KRW proves Hadamard/local-field obstructions at base points; Visser argues semiclassical reliability may fail before backreaction determines the outcome. None is a universal quantum-gravity prohibition.
entries.source: Hawking (1992); Kay–Radzikowski–Wald (1997); Visser (1997)
entries.notes: Original Hawking §§II–VI revisited, together with KRW Theorems 1/2 and Visser §§II–V; see SRC-003, SRC-055–057, NOTE-022–025 and research/field-note-003.md. Distinguish a QFT singular/undefined renormalized tensor from universal divergence of every stress component or proof of physical nonexistence.

entries.title: Quantum time-loop consistency can be modeled
entries.direction: Neutral
entries.strength: Mathematical / conditional
entries.question: Can a quantum formalism resolve a grandfather-type contradiction?
entries.finding: Deutsch modeled quantum systems interacting with closed timelike curves under self-consistency conditions; this does not establish branch travel.
entries.source: Deutsch · Quantum mechanics near closed timelike lines (1991)
entries.notes: Deutsch 1991 Eq.15-18 p.3203 establishes a finite-dimensional fixed-point consistency condition GIVEN an assumed CTC; a maximum-entropy selection is separately proposed p.3204. Politzer 1994 and Lloyd et al. 2011 offer mathematically different conditional prescriptions (abstracts examined). No observed gravitational CTC or branch count follows. Follow-up 2x2 NOT-loop toy Phi(rho)=XrhoX has both maximally mixed and pure-state fixed points, while a deterministic Boolean NOT loop cannot; conditional algebra, not proof of CTC existence.

entries.title: Many-worlds is a viable interpretation, not a verified branch census
entries.direction: Neutral
entries.strength: Interpretive framework
entries.question: Does quantum mechanics require multiple realized histories?
entries.finding: Everett, Bohmian particle configurations and objective-collapse models describe observed quantum outcomes with different physical ontologies; current reviews do not uniquely count actual branches.
entries.source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Many-Worlds Interpretation
entries.notes: See SRC-007/010/011/012/042/048/058–061; NOTE-026–030; field-note-004. The central test requires differing physical predictions, not a vote from Bell tests. S-002-R001: explicitly compared Bohm-Everett Born equivalence and objective-collapse parametric prediction limits; VC-008 remains editorial 59→59. S-002-R003: Everett original §5 note in proof explicitly assumes all branches are actual within the mathematical account; its additive positive measure is not independent experimental proof of history plurality. VC-009 editorial 59→59.

entries.title: Schrödinger's cat frames the measurement problem
entries.direction: Neutral
entries.strength: Pedagogical / conceptual
entries.question: How do quantum descriptions relate to definite observations?
entries.finding: The cat thought experiment highlights the measurement problem; its alternatives are interpreted differently by competing theories.
entries.source: Stanford Encyclopedia of Philosophy · Quantum Mechanics
entries.notes: A thought experiment is not an observation of competing universes.

entries.title: A chronology-horizon quantum-field obstruction has narrow theorem scope
entries.direction: Neither confirms nor refutes existence of multiple physical histories
entries.strength: Rigorous conditional field-theory theorem plus model-dependent reliability analysis; no direct experiment
entries.question: Does breakdown of ordinary field-theoretic assumptions on a compactly generated chronology horizon prove physically impossible time travel?
entries.finding: KRW's linear-field results establish breakdown of F-locality and Hadamard regularity at base points, not a universal no-time-machine theorem. Visser argues that semiclassical predictions may be unreliable near this region; special modeled cases evade large mean stress before reliability fails.
entries.source: Kay–Radzikowski–Wald (1997); Visser (1997)
entries.notes: Primary passage checks: SRC-055 (arXiv gr-qc/9603012, §§1/4/5/6), SRC-056 (arXiv gr-qc/9702041 §§II–V), SRC-057 (publisher abstract); NOTE-023–025; field-note-003. Not a proof that full quantum gravity forbids all CTCs.

entries.title: One observer record cannot establish how many physical histories are real
entries.direction: Neutral
entries.strength: Theories can have overlapping observable predictions
entries.question: Does our physical universe contain one actual timeline or multiple physically real outcome histories?
entries.finding: One outcome stream is observed by an individual. Everettian, Bohmian and objective-collapse theories differ in ontology while sharing much empirical quantum behavior; certain collapse dynamics can be tested conditionally.
entries.source: Everett 1957, Bohm 1952, GRW 1986, Zurek 2003, loophole-free Bell 2015
entries.notes: SRC-007/010/011/012/042/048/058–061; NOTE-026–030 and field-note-004. Bell tests are not proof of branching. R006 full-source batch in research/full-study-batch-001.md, NOTE-033–042, SRC-008/012/020/044/045/047/064 and complementary SRC-002/003/062; 10 completed literature reviews, not proof of branch ontology. S-002-R001: explicitly compared Bohm-Everett Born equivalence and objective-collapse parametric prediction limits; VC-008 remains editorial 59→59. S-002-R003: Everett original §5 note in proof explicitly assumes all branches are actual within the mathematical account; its additive positive measure is not independent experimental proof of history plurality. entries.title: Everett versus quantum-equilibrium Bohm predicts the same ordinary Born measurements
entries.status: Empirically equivalent under matched unitary/equilibrium assumptions
entries.direction: Neutral
entries.strength: Whole original Bohm 1952 Parts I/II, Hensen 2016 whole main paper, Everett source comparison
entries.question: Do ordinary quantum probabilities, decoherence or Bell violations reveal the count of physically real quantum histories?
entries.finding: Bohmian mechanics with one actual particle configuration and ρ=|ψ|² reproduces standard quantum probabilities and typical Everettian unitary measurement data. A measured Bell locality violation does not exclude explicitly nonlocal Bohm. Distinguishing the actual histories requires a model-dependent operational difference absent from this comparison.
entries.source: Bohm I/II (1952), Everett (1957) and Hensen et al. (2016)
entries.place: Foundational theoretical comparison, no claimed geographic detection
entries.notes: research/ontology-predictions-S002-R001.md; research/full-study-batch-002.md. Original Bohm I/II and Hensen second Bell main texts critically studied; Everett original publisher abstract only. Second Hensen run complete p=.061; pooled p=.017 or .0080 under different methods. 2×2 matrix educational. S-002-R003: Everett original §5 note in proof explicitly assumes all branches are actual within the mathematical account; its additive positive measure is not independent experimental proof of history plurality. VC-009 editorial 59→59.

entries.title: Objective-collapse dynamics face explicit molecular, force-noise and X-ray parameter tests
entries.status: Benchmark Markovian CSL regions experimentally excluded under specified assumptions; other collapse dynamics unresolved
entries.direction: Neutral
entries.strength: Complete 2026 XENONnT main primary article critically read; published 90% CL CSL/DP limits, 9.1σ benchmark under author's analysis; not independently reproduced likelihood
entries.question: Do observed data support stochastic collapse beyond ordinary unitary dynamics with environmental decoherence?
entries.finding: XENONnT found no significant 1–140 keV collapse-X-ray excess in 1.16 tonne-year exposure and published 90% CL CSL λ/rC²<3.0×10^-3 s^-1 m^-2. Under Markovian white-noise CSL a GRW-associated benchmark (λ=10^-16 s^-1, rC=10^-7m) is reported 9.1σ from best-fit; DP R0>4.9×10^-10m at 90% CL. This excludes a specified dynamical-model slice, NOT all GRW/CSL/one-history ontologies or multiple histories.
entries.source: XENON Collaboration, Phys Rev Lett 136 120201 (published March 23 2026)
entries.place: XENONnT experiment (exact detector coordinates not verified here)
entries.locationType: Physical experiment + later analytic constraints; no plotted coordinates
entries.notes: XENONnT original March 2026 publisher states ~100-fold improvement for benchmark CSL and factor five for DP with electron/proton cancellation; full confidence/likelihood contours not read. LISA abstract gives λ_CSL≤8.3×10^-11/s at rC=10^-7m. Projected underground sensitivity is not achieved measurement. Source depth NOTE-047–049. S-002-R005 original entire seven-page main text read and original Figs1/2 examined. Radiation model supplement/raw data were NOT independently rerun. Authors' 9.1σ is not a reproduced statistic, and applies to Markovian CSL with GRW-associated parameter values, not proof discrete GRW dynamics falsified.

entries.title: Published germanium Poisson posterior and LISA noise collapse limits independently reconstructed from printed aggregate data
entries.status: Two published parameter bound equations reproduced, with exact source prior conventions and independent numerical checks; full raw detector/simulation not replicated
entries.question: Can we independently reproduce a quantitative CSL exclusion, retaining source statistical methods and geometry rather than trusting plotted curves?
entries.finding: Germanium 2021 source z_c=576, z_b=506, coefficient 2.0986 and BOTH paper +1 pseudocounts give Gamma(577,1) 95% mean 617.071, a 95% Bayesian λ upper 5.19732362463e-13/s at rC=1e-7m (publisher 5.2e-13). LISA 2024 reported Brownian PSD uncertainty 0.075 femtometre²/s⁴/Hz and geometry give λ upper 8.36417404452e-11/s (source 8.3e-11). XENON 2026 90%-CL λ/rC²<0.003 implies λ<3e-17/s at rC=1e-7m (conversion, NOT own detector fit). Source-validated constraints are not 3 independent same-level likelihoods and cannot be multiplied to claim many worlds.
entries.source: Donadi et al., EPJC 81 773 (2021); Dai/Miao/Ma arXiv:2411.17588 (2024); XENON Collaboration PRL 136 120201 (2026)
entries.direction: Independent source-input statistical/mathematical reproduction strengthens parameter-domain conclusion; zero differentiation of Everett vs equilibrium Bohm history count
entries.strength: Germanium Bayesian 95% aggregated-count quantile reproduced; LISA published summary-noise conversion reproduced; XENON dimensional conversion only, original 9.1 sigma not replicated
entries.locationType: No experiment geolocation established by numerical reproduction; original cited detector sources retain their site context
entries.place: Multiple distinct apparatus; not one geolocated experiment
entries.notes: The paper's Eq11 adds 1 to BOTH z_b and z_s, so correct total offset=508 and λ=5.1973e-13. An interim result wrongly subtracting only 507 (5.245e-13) was corrected, documented, and regression-tested. Gamma posterior is Bayesian with fixed background; physical λ>=0 truncation shifts bound ~0.016%, while artificial ±25 background count sensitivity shifts ~4.006e-13 to 6.389e-13; that is NOT a validated systematic error bar. LISA trans low-rC λ upper scales inverse r², unlike X-ray radiation λ upper proportional r². Full angular LISA and molecular CSL numerics not reconstructed. Do not combine different CL/credible/noise-attribution upper limits.

entries.title: Born-rule collider tests are conditionally discriminating while equilibrium Bohm and Everett pointer likelihoods match
entries.kind: Theoretical model comparison and existing collider consistency check
entries.status: Prospective measurement gate with null-compatible tau helicity and formal equal-likelihood obstruction
entries.question: Do high-energy spin/polarisation counts distinguish one actual Bohmian history from Everett branches?
entries.finding: Valentini–Varma derived optional nonequilibrium angular deviations, with ideal 3sigma 1% target N>=360000 clean photons at pi/8; existing CMS tau helicity mean -0.144±0.015 vs Born -0.1472±0.0016 yields approx 0.21sigma, consistent with Born. Norsen analyses pilot-wave equilibrium where rho=|Psi|² and one pointer configuration reproduces unitary Born record statistics. Thus this data cannot distinguish Everett from equilibrium Bohm; genuine anomaly could constrain specified extra nonequilibrium models, not automatically settle actual branch ontology.
entries.source: Valentini & Varma (2025), Norsen (2018), source-examined collider inputs cited in former
entries.direction: No observed departure from Born or Everett-vs-Bohm equilibrium discriminator; original full-text theoretical and feasibility checks added
entries.strength: Complete original main texts plus arithmetic from source summary, collider raw likelihood unverified
entries.place: Multiple papers and collider datasets; no new coordinate claimed
entries.locationType: Theoretical and reused experimental data, not a new field experiment
entries.notes: The proposed photon count and ta[u] constraints are conditional: detector efficiency/polarimetry and background-trained Born MC selection can hide or mimic departures. Matching Everett and Bohm requires quantum equilibrium. See research/full-study-batch-004-one-many-Born-R010.md

entries.title: Flux-qubit control-calibrated coherence rejects an operational macroscopic eigenstate-mixture bound, not one actual history
entries.kind: Experimental result / explicitly scoped macrorealism rejection
entries.status: Published main experiment source-verified; rounded-source numerical significance independently rechecked
entries.question: Does a superconducting circuit show nonclassical disturbance exceeding classically measured controls, and does this identify multiple physically actual histories?
entries.finding: Knee et al. 2016 (Nature Communications 7:13253) report 7×10^6 trials per data point on a flux qubit and Fig 2 disturbance d_g=-0.026612±0.000438, d_e=+0.015884±0.000609, d_rho=-0.089788±0.000612. Our re-evaluation from original six displayed means/errors gives d_rho-d_g=-0.063176 and propagated significance 83.91 standard deviations (~84 as paper). Under its Eq7 no-extra-preparation-contextuality convex-control macrorealist class, d_rho falls outside [d_g,d_e]; a genuine conditional model-class exclusion, but compatible with Everett as well as one-configuration Bohmian equilibrium. No Everett branch is detected.
entries.source: Knee et al., Nature Communications (2016) main article, Fig 2c–d, Eqs 4–7, Methods and source PDF p1–5
entries.direction: Strengthens specific operational macroscopic-coherence claim only; no change in central real-histories dial
entries.strength: Original complete main article + independently recomputed statistics from published rounded means; no raw repeated-trial or supplement reanalysis
entries.place: Superconducting flux qubit laboratory; exact site coordinate not independently substantiated
entries.locationType: Physics apparatus publication attribution only; do not geolocate device from authors' institutional affiliations
entries.notes: Measurement pulses and preparation-conditioned disturbance bound may not cover all hidden-variable state spaces. Statistical '84σ' is relative to this experiment's assumptions and reported uncertainties, NOT likelihood ratio or odds favoring multiple physically real histories. See research/full-study-batch-005-macrorealism-R011.md.
